questions.stem: Preamble to Code and Standards most likely states:

options.A: Code of Ethics and Standards of Professional Conduct are fundamental to values of CFA Institute and essential to achieving its mission.
options.B: The Preamble states that the Standards are aspirational goals that members should strive toward but need not attain. That specification would be used as-is, with no forward-looking overlay.
options.C: The Preamble limits the Code's applicability to members employed by investment management firms.

rationales.A:
Full statement: Code of Ethics and Standards of Professional Conduct are fundamental to values of CFA Institute and essential to achieving its mission; since their creation in 1960s, Code and Standards have promoted integrity of CFA Institute members and served as model for measuring ethics of investment professionals globally, regardless of job function, cultural differences, or local laws and regulations; all CFA Institute members and CFA candidates have personal responsibility to embrace and uphold provisions of Code and Standards and are encouraged to notify their employer of this responsibility; violations may result in disciplinary sanctions by CFA Institute including revocation of membership, revocation of candidacy in CFA Program, and revocation of right to use CFA designation.

Correct. Per the reading Preamble: 'The CFA Institute Code of Ethics and Standards of Professional Conduct are fundamental to the values of CFA Institute and essential to achieving its mission... Since their creation in the 1960s, the Code and Standards have promoted the integrity of CFA Institute members and served as a model for measuring the ethics of investment professionals globally, regardless of job function, cultural differences, or local laws and regulations. All CFA Institute members (including holders of the Chartered Financial Analyst® [CFA] designation) and CFA candidates have the personal responsibility to embrace and uphold the provisions of the Code and Standards and are encouraged to notify their employer of this responsibility. Violations may result in disciplinary sanctions by CFA Institute. Sanctions can include revocation of membership, revocation of candidacy in the CFA Program, and revocation of the right to use the CFA designation.'
rationales.B: Incorrect. The Code and Standards are binding on members and candidates, not merely aspirational.
rationales.C: Incorrect. The Code applies to all members and candidates regardless of employer type.

questions.stem: Code of Ethics first principle most likely requires Members and Candidates to:

options.A: The first principle addresses only conduct toward clients, excluding colleagues and the public.
options.B: Act with integrity, competence, diligence, and respect and in an ethical manner with the public, clients, prospective clients, employers, employees, colleagues in the investment profession, and other participants in the global capital markets.
options.C: The first principle requires placing the employer's interests above those of clients and market integrity.

rationales.A: Incorrect. The first principle explicitly names the public, clients, prospects, employers, employees, and colleagues.
rationales.B: Correct. Per the Code of Ethics first principle: 'Act with integrity, competence, diligence, and respect and in an ethical manner with the public, clients, prospective clients, employers, employees, colleagues in the investment profession, and other participants in the global capital markets.'
rationales.C: Incorrect. The Code requires integrity and ethical conduct toward the public, clients, employers, employees, and colleagues; client interests and market integrity come before personal or employer advantage.

questions.stem: Code of Ethics second principle most likely requires:

options.A: Place the interests of their employer above the integrity of the investment profession.
options.B: Place the integrity of the investment profession and the interests of clients above their own personal interests.
options.C: Place their own reputation and their firm's profitability above the interests of clients.

rationales.A: Incorrect; the second principle places the integrity of the profession and client interests above personal interests, not employer interests above the profession.
rationales.B: Correct. Per the Code of Ethics second principle: 'Place the integrity of the investment profession and the interests of clients above their own personal interests.'
rationales.C: Incorrect; client interests and the integrity of the profession must come before personal or firm interests, which reverses this statement.

questions.stem: Code of Ethics third principle most likely requires:

options.A: The third principle requires maximizing returns for clients regardless of the level of care exercised.
options.B: Independent professional judgment may be subordinated to the consensus view of the firm's research committee.
options.C: Use reasonable care and exercise independent professional judgment when conducting investment analysis, making investment recommendations, taking investment actions, and engaging in other professional activities.

rationales.A: Incorrect. The principle concerns reasonable care and independent judgment, not a return-maximization guarantee.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Judgment must remain independent; committee consensus does not replace it.
rationales.C: Correct. Per the Code of Ethics third principle: 'Use reasonable care and exercise independent professional judgment when conducting investment analysis, making investment recommendations, taking investment actions, and engaging in other professional activities.'

questions.stem: Code of Ethics fourth principle most likely requires:

options.A: The fourth principle concerns only one's own practice and imposes no duty regarding the conduct of others.
options.B: Practice and encourage others to practice in a professional and ethical manner that will reflect credit on themselves and the profession.
options.C: The fourth principle requires reporting all observed violations to securities regulators.

rationales.A: Incorrect. Members must also ENCOURAGE OTHERS to practice professionally and ethically.
rationales.B: Correct. Per the Code of Ethics fourth principle: 'Practice and encourage others to practice in a professional and ethical manner that will reflect credit on themselves and the profession.'
rationales.C: Incorrect. The principle concerns practicing and encouraging ethical practice, not a regulatory reporting mandate.

questions.stem: Code of Ethics fifth principle most likely requires:

options.A: Promote the integrity and viability of the global capital markets for the ultimate benefit of society.
options.B: Promote the growth and profitability of the investment management industry.
options.C: Promote the integrity of the global capital markets solely for the benefit of CFA Institute members. That specification would be used as-is, with no forward-looking overlay.

rationales.A: Correct. Per the Code of Ethics fifth principle: 'Promote the integrity and viability of the global capital markets for the ultimate benefit of society.' Note per Solution 2: this reflects the role that capital markets have in society as a whole — versions omitting 'for the ultimate benefit of society' are incomplete.
rationales.B: Incorrect; the fifth principle promotes the integrity and viability of the capital markets for society, not the profitability of the industry.
rationales.C: Incorrect; markets' integrity is promoted for the ultimate benefit of society, and omitting that phrase in favor of members is the incomplete version.

questions.stem: Code of Ethics sixth principle most likely requires:

options.A: The sixth principle requires attaining a specified number of continuing education credits annually.
options.B: The sixth principle concerns maintaining one's own competence only, with no reference to other professionals. That specification would be used as-is, with no forward-looking overlay.
options.C: Maintain and improve their professional competence and strive to maintain and improve the competence of other investment professionals.

rationales.A: Incorrect. No specific credit count is mandated by the Code's principles.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Members must also strive to maintain and improve the competence of OTHER investment professionals.
rationales.C: Correct. Per the Code of Ethics sixth principle: 'Maintain and improve their professional competence and strive to maintain and improve the competence of other investment professionals.'

questions.stem: Standard I: Professionalism most likely has how many subsections and covers:

options.A: Five subsections — I(A) Knowledge of the Law, I(B) Independence and Objectivity, I(C) Misrepresentation, I(D) Misconduct, I(E) Competence.
options.B: Standard I includes a subsection on Fair Dealing.
options.C: Standard I contains four subsections, ending with I(D) Misconduct.

rationales.A: Correct. Per the Standards of Professional Conduct: 'i. PROFESSIONALISM: A. Knowledge of the Law; B. Independence and Objectivity; C. Misrepresentation; D. Misconduct; E. Competence.'
rationales.B: Incorrect. Fair Dealing is Standard III(B), under Duties to Clients.
rationales.C: Incorrect. There are five subsections; I(E) Competence completes the list.

questions.stem: Standard I(A) Knowledge of the Law most likely requires:

options.A: Members and candidates need only comply with the local law of the jurisdiction where they work and may disregard the Code and Standards wherever local law is silent.
options.B: Understand and comply with all applicable laws, rules, and regulations (including CFA Institute Code of Ethics and Standards of Professional Conduct) of any government, regulatory organization, licensing agency, or professional association governing their professional activities.
options.C: Compliance requires members to acquire detailed expert knowledge of the laws of every government, regulatory organization, and agency to which they could conceivably be subject.

rationales.A: Incorrect. Where law is less strict or silent, the Code and Standards govern.
rationales.B:
Full statement: understand and comply with all applicable laws, rules, and regulations (including CFA Institute Code of Ethics and Standards of Professional Conduct) of any government, regulatory organization, licensing agency, or professional association governing their professional activities; in event of conflict, must comply with the MORE STRICT law, rule, or regulation; must NOT knowingly participate or assist in and must DISSOCIATE from any violation of such laws, rules, or regulations.

Correct. Per Standard I(A): 'Members and Candidates must understand and comply with all applicable laws, rules, and regulations (including the CFA Institute Code of Ethics and Standards of Professional Conduct) of any government, regulatory organization, licensing agency, or professional association governing their professional activities. In the event of conflict, Members and Candidates must comply with the more strict law, rule, or regulation. Members and Candidates must not knowingly participate or assist in and must dissociate from any violation of such laws, rules, or regulations.'
rationales.C: Incorrect. The duty is to UNDERSTAND and comply with applicable law; expert mastery of all laws is not required.

questions.stem: Standard I(B) Independence and Objectivity most likely requires:

options.A: Must refuse every gift or benefit of any value under all circumstances.
options.B: May accept any gift from a client, since gifts from clients cannot compromise independence and objectivity.
options.C: Use reasonable care and judgment to achieve and maintain independence and objectivity in their professional activities.

rationales.A: Incorrect; the standard prohibits only gifts that could compromise objectivity, not every gift — modest or token items may be permissible.
rationales.B: Incorrect; members must not accept any gift or benefit that reasonably could be expected to compromise independence and objectivity, including gifts from clients.
rationales.C:
Full statement: use reasonable care and judgment to achieve and maintain independence and objectivity in their professional activities; must NOT offer, solicit, or accept any gift, benefit, compensation, or consideration that reasonably could be expected to compromise their own or another's independence and objectivity.

Correct. Per Standard I(B): 'Members and Candidates must use reasonable care and judgment to achieve and maintain independence and objectivity in their professional activities. Members and Candidates must not offer, solicit, or accept any gift, benefit, compensation, or consideration that reasonably could be expected to compromise their own or another's independence and objectivity.'

questions.stem: Standard I(C) Misrepresentation most likely requires:

options.A: Standard I(C) prohibits only intentional misrepresentations made in written research reports.
options.B: Standard I(C) permits misrepresentations provided they are corrected within a reasonable period.
options.C: Must NOT knowingly make any misrepresentations relating to investment analysis, recommendations, actions, or other professional activities.

rationales.A: Incorrect. The prohibition covers any knowing misrepresentation across analysis, recommendations, actions, or other professional activities — not only written reports.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Knowing misrepresentation is prohibited outright; later correction does not authorize it.
rationales.C: Correct. Per Standard I(C): 'Members and Candidates must not knowingly make any misrepresentations relating to investment analysis, recommendations, actions, or other professional activities.'

questions.stem: Standard I(D) Misconduct most likely requires:

options.A: Standard I(D) applies only to conduct occurring on the employer's premises during business hours.
options.B: Must NOT engage in any professional conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, or deceit or commit any act that reflects adversely on their professional reputation, integrity, or competence.
options.C: Standard I(D) is limited to conduct resulting in criminal convictions for fraud.

rationales.A: Incorrect. Misconduct covers professional conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, or deceit wherever it occurs.
rationales.B: Correct. Per Standard I(D): 'Members and Candidates must not engage in any professional conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, or deceit or commit any act that reflects adversely on their professional reputation, integrity, or competence.'
rationales.C: Incorrect. No conviction is required; acts reflecting adversely on professional reputation, integrity, or competence are covered.

questions.stem: Standard I(E) Competence most likely requires:

options.A: Must act with and maintain the competence necessary to fulfill their professional responsibilities.
options.B: Must complete a mandatory minimum number of continuing education hours each year. That specification would be used as-is, with no forward-looking overlay.
options.C: Must hold the CFA charter before providing any investment analysis or advice.

rationales.A: Correct. Per Standard I(E): 'Members and Candidates must act with and maintain the competence necessary to fulfill their professional responsibilities.'
rationales.B: Incorrect; the standard requires actual competence, not a prescribed number of continuing education hours.
rationales.C: Incorrect; Standard I(E) requires maintaining the competence necessary for one's responsibilities, not possession of the CFA charter.

questions.stem: Standard II: Integrity of Capital Markets most likely subsections:

options.A: Three subsections — II(A) Material Nonpublic Information, II(B) Market Manipulation, and II(C) Fair Dealing.
options.B: Two subsections — II(A) Material Nonpublic Information and II(B) Market Manipulation.
options.C: One subsection — II(A) Material Nonpublic Information.

rationales.A: Incorrect; Standard II has only two subsections — Fair Dealing is Standard III(B), under Duties to Clients.
rationales.B: Correct. Per the Standards of Professional Conduct: 'ii. INTEGRITY OF CAPITAL MARKETS: A. Material Nonpublic Information; B. Market Manipulation.'
rationales.C: Incorrect; Standard II has two subsections, also including II(B) Market Manipulation.

questions.stem: Standard II(A) Material Nonpublic Information most likely requires:

options.A: Members possessing material nonpublic information may act on it provided they disclose the trade to their employer.
options.B: The prohibition applies only to information obtained directly from company insiders.
options.C: Members and Candidates who possess material nonpublic information that could affect the value of an investment must NOT act or cause others to act on the information.

rationales.A: Incorrect. Acting (or causing others to act) on MNPI is prohibited; employer disclosure does not cure it.
rationales.B: Incorrect. The source of the information is irrelevant; possession of MNPI triggers the prohibition.
rationales.C: Correct. Per Standard II(A): 'Members and Candidates who possess material nonpublic information that could affect the value of an investment must not act or cause others to act on the information.' Per Solution 5: 'inappropriately causing others to act' violates Standard II(A).

questions.stem: Standard II(B) Market Manipulation most likely requires:

options.A: Must NOT engage in practices that distort prices or artificially inflate trading volume with the intent to mislead market participants.
options.B: Standard II(B) prohibits all trading strategies that move market prices, regardless of intent.
options.C: Standard II(B) applies only to spreading false rumors, not to transaction-based manipulation.

rationales.A: Correct. Per Standard II(B): 'Members and Candidates must not engage in practices that distort prices or artificially inflate trading volume with the intent to mislead market participants.'
rationales.B: Incorrect. Intent to mislead is the key element; legitimate trading that moves prices is not manipulation.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Both information-based and transaction-based manipulation (distorting prices or inflating volume) are covered.

questions.stem: Standard III: Duties to Clients most likely subsections:

options.A: Six subsections — beginning with III(A) Loyalty, Prudence, and Care and ending with III(F) Referral Fees.
options.B: Five subsections — III(A) Loyalty, Prudence, and Care.
options.C: Four subsections — III(A) Loyalty, Prudence, and Care; III(B) Fair Dealing; III(C) Suitability; III(D) Preservation of Confidentiality.

rationales.A: Incorrect; Standard III has five subsections and Referral Fees is Standard VI(C), under Conflicts of Interest.
rationales.B:
Full statement: five subsections — III(A) Loyalty, Prudence, and Care; III(B) Fair Dealing; III(C) Suitability; III(D) Performance Presentation; III(E) Preservation of Confidentiality.

Correct. Per the Standards of Professional Conduct: 'iii. DUTIES TO CLIENTS: A. Loyalty, Prudence, and Care; B. Fair Dealing; C. Suitability; D. Performance Presentation; E. Preservation of Confidentiality.'
rationales.C: Incorrect; Standard III has five subsections — this omits III(D) Performance Presentation.

questions.stem: Standard III(A) Loyalty, Prudence, and Care most likely requires:

options.A: Have a duty of loyalty to their employer that takes precedence over the interests of their clients.
options.B: Have a duty of loyalty to their clients and must act with reasonable care and exercise prudent judgment.
options.C: Guarantee a minimum rate of return to clients when exercising prudent judgment.

rationales.A: Incorrect; Standard III(A) requires placing clients' interests before the employer's or one's own — employer loyalty is the subject of Standard IV(A).
rationales.B:
Full statement: have a duty of loyalty to their clients and must act with reasonable care and exercise prudent judgment; must act for the benefit of their clients and place their clients' interests before their employer's or their own interests.

Correct. Per Standard III(A): 'Members and Candidates have a duty of loyalty to their clients and must act with reasonable care and exercise prudent judgment. Members and Candidates must act for the benefit of their clients and place their clients' interests before their employer's or their own interests.'
rationales.C: Incorrect; the duty is reasonable care and prudent judgment, not a guarantee of investment returns.

questions.stem: Standard III(B) Fair Dealing most likely requires:

options.A: Standard III(B) applies when making recommendations but not when taking investment action.
options.B: Must deal fairly and objectively with ALL clients when providing investment analysis, making investment recommendations, taking investment action, or engaging in other professional activities.
options.C: Fair dealing requires that all clients be treated equally, receiving identical recommendations and allocations. That specification would be used as-is, with no forward-looking overlay. Applied uniformly, it would bind at every horizon and every asset class.

rationales.A: Incorrect. Fair dealing expressly covers analysis, recommendations, investment action, and other professional activities.
rationales.B: Correct. Per Standard III(B): 'Members and Candidates must deal fairly and objectively with all clients when providing investment analysis, making investment recommendations, taking investment action, or engaging in other professional activities.'
rationales.C: Incorrect. The requirement is fair and objective dealing, not identical treatment; differing service levels are permissible if disclosed and not disadvantaging.

questions.stem: Standard III(C) Suitability requirements (advisory relationship) most likely:

options.A: When in advisory relationship with client, must make reasonable inquiry into client's or prospective client's investment experience, risk and return objectives, and financial constraints PRIOR to making any investment recommendation or taking investment action and must REASSESS and update this information REGULARLY.
options.B: A single suitability assessment performed at account opening satisfies Standard III(C) for the life of the relationship, with no obligation to update or reassess the information.
options.C: In an advisory relationship, the suitability inquiry applies only to fully discretionary accounts; nondiscretionary advisory clients require no assessment of experience, objectives, or constraints. That specification would be used as-is, with no forward-looking overlay. Applied uniformly, it would bind at every horizon and every asset class.

rationales.A:
Full statement: when in advisory relationship with client, must: (a) make reasonable inquiry into client's or prospective client's investment experience, risk and return objectives, and financial constraints PRIOR to making any investment recommendation or taking investment action and must REASSESS and update this information REGULARLY; (b) determine that investment is suitable to client's financial situation and consistent with client's written objectives, mandates, and constraints; (c) judge suitability of investments in the context of the client's total portfolio.

Correct. Per Standard III(C)(1): 'When Members and Candidates are in an advisory relationship with a client, they must: a. Make a reasonable inquiry into a client's or prospective client's investment experience, risk and return objectives, and financial constraints prior to making any investment recommendation or taking investment action and must reassess and update this information regularly. b. Determine that an investment is suitable to the client's financial situation and consistent with the client's written objectives, mandates, and constraints before making an investment recommendation or taking investment action. c. Judge the suitability of investments in the context of the client's total portfolio.'
rationales.B: Incorrect. The IPS and client circumstances must be reviewed and reassessed regularly, not just at inception.
rationales.C: Incorrect. The three-part inquiry applies whenever the member is in an advisory relationship.

questions.stem: Standard III(C) Suitability requirements (portfolio mandate) most likely:

options.A: Managers of a fund run to a stated mandate must tailor each holding to the personal circumstances of every fund investor. That specification would be used as-is, with no forward-looking overlay. Applied uniformly, it would bind at every horizon and every asset class.
options.B: Deviation from the stated mandate is permitted whenever the manager expects it to improve returns.
options.C: When responsible for managing portfolio to specific mandate, strategy, or style, must make ONLY investment recommendations or take ONLY investment actions that are consistent with stated objectives and constraints of the portfolio.

rationales.A: Incorrect. For a mandate, strategy, or style, suitability runs to consistency with the stated objectives, not to each investor's circumstances.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Only recommendations and actions consistent with the stated mandate are permitted; expected outperformance does not authorize drift.
rationales.C: Correct. Per Standard III(C)(2): 'When Members and Candidates are responsible for managing a portfolio to a specific mandate, strategy, or style, they must make only investment recommendations or take only investment actions that are consistent with the stated objectives and constraints of the portfolio.'

questions.stem: Standard III(D) Performance Presentation most likely requires:

options.A: Performance presentation obligations apply only to firms that claim GIPS compliance.
options.B: When communicating investment performance information, must make reasonable efforts to ensure that it is fair, accurate, and complete.
options.C: Brief performance communications are exempt from the fair, accurate, and complete requirement. That specification would be used as-is, with no forward-looking overlay.

rationales.A: Incorrect. Standard III(D) binds all members communicating performance, whether or not the firm claims GIPS compliance.
rationales.B: Correct. Per Standard III(D): 'When communicating investment performance information, Members and Candidates must make reasonable efforts to ensure that it is fair, accurate, and complete.'
rationales.C: Incorrect. Brevity does not excuse misleading presentation; reasonable efforts at fairness, accuracy, and completeness still apply.

questions.stem: Standard III(E) Preservation of Confidentiality exceptions most likely:

options.A: Must keep information about current, former, and prospective clients confidential UNLESS: (1) information concerns illegal activities on the part of the client or prospective client; (2) disclosure is required by law; or (3) the client or prospective client permits disclosure of the information.
options.B: Confidentiality obligations end when the client relationship terminates.
options.C: Client information must be kept confidential without exception, even when disclosure is required by law.

rationales.A:
Full statement: must keep information about current, former, and prospective clients confidential UNLESS: (1) information concerns illegal activities on the part of the client or prospective client; (2) disclosure is required by law; or (3) the client or prospective client permits disclosure of the information.

Correct. Per Standard III(E): 'Members and Candidates must keep information about current, former, and prospective clients confidential unless: 1. The information concerns illegal activities on the part of the client or prospective client, 2. Disclosure is required by law, or 3. The client or prospective client permits disclosure of the information.'
rationales.B: Incorrect. The duty covers current, former, and prospective clients.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Legally required disclosure is one of three exceptions, alongside illegal client activity and client permission.

questions.stem: Standard IV: Duties to Employers most likely subsections:

options.A: Two subsections — IV(A) Loyalty and IV(B) Responsibilities of Supervisors.
options.B: Three subsections — IV(A) Loyalty, IV(B) Additional Compensation Arrangements, IV(C) Responsibilities of Supervisors.
options.C: Four subsections — IV(A) Loyalty; IV(B) Additional Compensation Arrangements; IV(C) Responsibilities of Supervisors; IV(D) Referral Fees.

rationales.A: Incorrect; Standard IV has three subsections — this omits IV(B) Additional Compensation Arrangements.
rationales.B: Correct. Per the Standards of Professional Conduct: 'iv. DUTIES TO EMPLOYERS: A. Loyalty; B. Additional Compensation Arrangements; C. Responsibilities of Supervisors.'
rationales.C: Incorrect; Standard IV has three subsections and Referral Fees is Standard VI(C), under Conflicts of Interest.

questions.stem: Standard IV(A) Loyalty (to employer) most likely requires:

options.A: Standard IV(A) prohibits members from ever seeking employment with a competitor while still employed.
options.B: Loyalty to the employer requires members to comply with directives even when they involve violating the law. That specification would be used as-is, with no forward-looking overlay. Applied uniformly, it would bind at every horizon and every asset class.
options.C: In matters related to their employment, must act for benefit of their employer and NOT deprive their employer of the advantage of their skills and abilities, divulge confidential information, or otherwise cause harm to their employer.

rationales.A: Incorrect. Preparing to leave, including seeking other employment, is permitted so long as employer interests are not harmed and confidential information is not misused.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Employer loyalty never requires unethical or illegal action; the Code and law take precedence.
rationales.C: Correct. Per Standard IV(A): 'In matters related to their employment, Members and Candidates must act for the benefit of their employer and not deprive their employer of the advantage of their skills and abilities, divulge confidential information, or otherwise cause harm to their employer.' Solution 8: 'deprive their employer of their skills and abilities as related to their employment' is prohibited.

questions.stem: Standard IV(B) Additional Compensation Arrangements most likely requires:

options.A: Must NOT accept gifts, benefits, compensation, or consideration that competes with or might reasonably be expected to create conflict of interest with their employer's interest UNLESS they obtain WRITTEN CONSENT from ALL parties involved.
options.B: Verbal notification to a supervisor is sufficient consent for additional compensation arrangements.
options.C: Members may accept outside compensation that conflicts with the employer's interest provided it is disclosed after the fact.

rationales.A: Correct. Per Standard IV(B): 'Members and Candidates must not accept gifts, benefits, compensation, or consideration that competes with or might reasonably be expected to create a conflict of interest with their employer's interest unless they obtain written consent from all parties involved.'
rationales.B: Incorrect. Consent must be written and from all parties involved; verbal notice is insufficient.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Written consent from all parties involved must be obtained BEFORE accepting such arrangements.

questions.stem: Standard IV(C) Responsibilities of Supervisors most likely requires:

options.A: Must make reasonable efforts to ensure that anyone subject to their supervision or authority complies with applicable laws, rules, regulations, and the Code and Standards.
options.B: Supervisors are responsible only for detecting violations after they occur, not for preventing them. That specification would be used as-is, with no forward-looking overlay.
options.C: A supervisor who delegates supervisory duties thereby transfers away responsibility for compliance.

rationales.A: Correct. Per Standard IV(C): 'Members and Candidates must make reasonable efforts to ensure that anyone subject to their supervision or authority complies with applicable laws, rules, regulations, and the Code and Standards.'
rationales.B: Incorrect. Reasonable efforts include prevention — establishing and enforcing procedures — not merely after-the-fact detection.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Delegation does not relieve a supervisor of supervisory responsibility.

questions.stem: Standard V: Investment Analysis, Recommendations, and Actions most likely subsections:

options.A: Three subsections — V(A) Diligence and Reasonable Basis, V(B) Communication with Clients and Prospective Clients, V(C) Record Retention.
options.B: Standard V includes a subsection governing Referral Fees.
options.C: Standard V contains two subsections: Diligence and Reasonable Basis, and Record Retention.

rationales.A: Correct. Per the Standards of Professional Conduct: 'v. INVESTMENT ANALYSIS, RECOMMENDATIONS, AND ACTIONS: A. Diligence and Reasonable Basis; B. Communication with Clients and Prospective Clients; C. Record Retention.'
rationales.B: Incorrect. Referral Fees is Standard VI(C), under Conflicts of Interest.
rationales.C: Incorrect. There are three subsections; Communication with Clients and Prospective Clients is V(B).

questions.stem: Standard V(A) Diligence and Reasonable Basis most likely requires:

options.A: Diligence obligations can be fully satisfied by relying on the sponsor's marketing materials for a recommended product.
options.B: Must: (1) exercise diligence, independence, and thoroughness in analyzing investments, making investment recommendations, and taking investment actions.
options.C: Standard V(A) requires a reasonable basis for sell recommendations only, not for purchases.

rationales.A: Incorrect. Diligence, independence, and thoroughness require analysis beyond promotional material.
rationales.B:
Full statement: must: (1) exercise diligence, independence, and thoroughness in analyzing investments, making investment recommendations, and taking investment actions; (2) have reasonable and adequate basis, supported by appropriate research and investigation, for any investment analysis, recommendation, or action.

Correct. Per Standard V(A): 'Members and Candidates must: 1. Exercise diligence, independence, and thoroughness in analyzing investments, making investment recommendations, and taking investment actions. 2. Have a reasonable and adequate basis, supported by appropriate research and investigation, for any investment analysis, recommendation, or action.'
rationales.C: Incorrect. The requirement applies to all investment analysis, recommendations, and actions, in both directions.

questions.stem: Standard V(B) Communication with Clients most likely requires (services/costs):

options.A: The nature of services must be described only in the initial engagement letter and never updated.
options.B: Must disclose to clients and prospective clients the nature of services provided along with information about costs to client associated with those services.
options.C: Disclosure of costs is required only upon a client's written request.

rationales.A: Incorrect. Disclosure obligations are ongoing, not confined to the initial engagement document.
rationales.B: Correct. Per Standard V(B)(1): 'Disclose to clients and prospective clients the nature of the services provided, along with information about the costs to the client associated with those services.'
rationales.C: Incorrect. The nature of services and associated client costs must be affirmatively disclosed.

questions.stem: Standard V(B)(2) Communication — investment process most likely requires:

options.A: Disclosure of the investment process is required only for quantitative strategies.
options.B: Members must disclose the proprietary details and full model code of their investment process. That specification would be used as-is, with no forward-looking overlay. Applied uniformly, it would bind at every horizon and every asset class. No cycle overlay would be allowed to lift or cut that bound.
options.C: Must disclose to clients and prospective clients basic format and general principles of investment processes they use to analyze investments, select securities, and construct portfolios and must PROMPTLY DISCLOSE any changes that might materially affect those processes.

rationales.A: Incorrect. The disclosure obligation applies to whatever process is used, quantitative or fundamental.
rationales.B: Incorrect. The requirement is the basic format and general principles of the process, not proprietary detail.
rationales.C: Correct. Per Standard V(B)(2): 'Disclose to clients and prospective clients the basic format and general principles of the investment processes they use to analyze investments, select securities, and construct portfolios and must promptly disclose any changes that might materially affect those processes.'

questions.stem: Standard V(B)(3) Communication — limitations and risks most likely requires:

options.A: Only risks that have historically materialized must be disclosed to clients.
options.B: Must disclose to clients and prospective clients significant limitations and risks associated with the investment process.
options.C: Limitations of the investment process may be omitted if they are described in the fund's offering documents.

rationales.A: Incorrect. Significant limitations and risks of the process must be disclosed, not just realized ones.
rationales.B: Correct. Per Standard V(B)(3): 'Disclose to clients and prospective clients significant limitations and risks associated with the investment process.'
rationales.C: Incorrect. The member's disclosure duty to clients is not discharged by references buried in offering documents.

questions.stem: Standard V(B)(4) Communication — important factors most likely:

options.A: Use reasonable judgment in identifying which factors are important to their investment analyses, recommendations, or actions and include those factors in communications with clients and prospective clients.
options.B: All factors considered in the analysis must be included in client communications, regardless of importance.
options.C: Factor selection for communications may be driven by which factors best support the recommendation.

rationales.A: Correct. Per Standard V(B)(4): 'Use reasonable judgment in identifying which factors are important to their investment analyses, recommendations, or actions and include those factors in communications with clients and prospective clients.'
rationales.B: Incorrect. Reasonable judgment identifies the IMPORTANT factors; exhaustive inclusion is not required.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Selecting only supportive factors would mislead; judgment must be exercised objectively.

questions.stem: Standard V(B)(5) Communication — fact vs opinion most likely requires:

options.A: Distinguish between fact and opinion in the presentation of investment analysis and recommendations.
options.B: Present only verifiable facts and omit all opinions from investment recommendations.
options.C: Guarantee the accuracy of all opinions expressed in investment analysis and recommendations.

rationales.A: Correct. Per Standard V(B)(5): 'Distinguish between fact and opinion in the presentation of investment analysis and recommendations.'
rationales.B: Incorrect; opinions may be presented — they must simply be distinguished from fact.
rationales.C: Incorrect; the requirement is to distinguish fact from opinion, not to guarantee that opinions prove accurate.

questions.stem: Standard V(C) Record Retention most likely requires:

options.A: Records supporting recommendations may be discarded once the recommendation is communicated to clients.
options.B: Must develop and maintain appropriate records to support their investment analyses, recommendations, actions, and other investment-related communications with clients and prospective clients.
options.C: Record retention is solely the firm's obligation and imposes no responsibility on individual members.

rationales.A: Incorrect. Records must be developed and MAINTAINED to support analyses, recommendations, actions, and communications.
rationales.B: Correct. Per Standard V(C): 'Members and Candidates must develop and maintain appropriate records to support their investment analyses, recommendations, actions, and other investment-related communications with clients and prospective clients.'
rationales.C: Incorrect. The develop-and-maintain obligation is placed on members and candidates themselves.

questions.stem: Standard VI: Conflicts of Interest most likely subsections:

options.A: Four subsections — VI(A) Avoid or Disclose Conflicts; VI(B) Priority of Transactions; VI(C) Referral Fees; VI(D) Additional Compensation Arrangements.
options.B: Three subsections — VI(A) Avoid or Disclose Conflicts; VI(B) Priority of Transactions; VI(C) Referral Fees.
options.C: Two subsections — VI(A) Avoid or Disclose Conflicts and VI(B) Priority of Transactions.

rationales.A: Incorrect; Standard VI has three subsections and Additional Compensation Arrangements is Standard IV(B), under Duties to Employers.
rationales.B: Correct. Per the Standards of Professional Conduct: 'vi. CONFLICTS OF INTEREST: A. Avoid or Disclose Conflicts; B. Priority of Transactions; C. Referral Fees.'
rationales.C: Incorrect; Standard VI has three subsections — this omits VI(C) Referral Fees.

questions.stem: Standard VI(A) Avoid or Disclose Conflicts most likely requires:

options.A: Disclosure is required only for conflicts that have already impaired objectivity, not potential conflicts.
options.B: Conflicts of interest need only be disclosed internally to compliance, not to clients or other affected parties. That specification would be used as-is, with no forward-looking overlay. Applied uniformly, it would bind at every horizon and every asset class.
options.C: Must AVOID or make full and fair disclosure of all matters that could reasonably be expected to impair their independence and objectivity and interfere with respective duties to their clients, prospective clients, and employer.

rationales.A: Incorrect. Matters that COULD REASONABLY BE EXPECTED to impair independence and objectivity are covered — potential conflicts included.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Full and fair disclosure must reach the parties whose interests could be affected — clients, prospects, and employer as relevant.
rationales.C:
Full statement: must AVOID or make full and fair disclosure of all matters that could reasonably be expected to impair their independence and objectivity and interfere with respective duties to their clients, prospective clients, and employer; must ensure that such disclosures are prominent, are delivered in plain language, and communicate the relevant information effectively.

Correct. Per Standard VI(A): 'Members and Candidates must avoid or make full and fair disclosure of all matters that could reasonably be expected to impair their independence and objectivity and interfere with respective duties to their clients, prospective clients, and employer. Members and Candidates must ensure that such disclosures are prominent, are delivered in plain language, and communicate the relevant information effectively.'

questions.stem: Standard VI(B) Priority of Transactions most likely requires:

options.A: Standard VI(B) prohibits members from ever trading securities held in client accounts.
options.B: Investment transactions for clients and employers must have PRIORITY over investment transactions in which a Member or Candidate is the beneficial owner.
options.C: Personal transactions may be executed simultaneously with client orders provided prices are identical.

rationales.A: Incorrect. Personal investment in the same securities is permitted once clients and employers have had priority.
rationales.B: Correct. Per Standard VI(B): 'Investment transactions for clients and employers must have priority over investment transactions in which a Member or Candidate is the beneficial owner.'
rationales.C: Incorrect. Client and employer transactions take priority; simultaneous personal execution can still disadvantage clients.

questions.stem: Standard VI(C) Referral Fees most likely requires:

options.A: Must disclose to their employer, clients, and prospective clients, as appropriate, any compensation, consideration, or benefit received from or paid to others for the recommendation of products or services.
options.B: Referral fees must be disclosed only when the referred client asks about compensation arrangements. That specification would be used as-is, with no forward-looking overlay. Applied uniformly, it would bind at every horizon and every asset class.
options.C: Referral fee disclosure applies to cash payments but not to soft benefits or in-kind consideration.

rationales.A: Correct. Per Standard VI(C): 'Members and Candidates must disclose to their employer, clients, and prospective clients, as appropriate, any compensation, consideration, or benefit received from or paid to others for the recommendation of products or services.'
rationales.B: Incorrect. Disclosure must be made affirmatively to employer, clients, and prospective clients as appropriate.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Any compensation, consideration, or BENEFIT received or paid for recommendations is covered.

questions.stem: Standard VII: Responsibilities as CFA Institute Member or CFA Candidate most likely subsections:

options.A: Standard VII includes a subsection on Performance Presentation.
options.B: Standard VII contains a single subsection addressing conduct during CFA examinations. That specification would be used as-is, with no forward-looking overlay.
options.C: Two subsections — VII(A) Conduct as Participants in CFA Institute Programs and VII(B) Reference to CFA Institute, the CFA Designation, and the CFA Program.

rationales.A: Incorrect. Performance Presentation is Standard III(D).
rationales.B: Incorrect. There are two subsections: VII(A) program conduct and VII(B) reference to the Institute, designation, and program.
rationales.C: Correct. Per the Standards of Professional Conduct: 'vii. RESPONSIBILITIES AS A CFA INSTITUTE MEMBER OR CFA CANDIDATE: A. Conduct as Participants in CFA Institute Programs; B. Reference to CFA Institute, the CFA Designation, and the CFA Program.'

questions.stem: Standard VII(A) Conduct as Participants in CFA Institute Programs most likely:

options.A: Must NOT engage in any conduct that compromises the reputation or integrity of CFA Institute or the CFA designation or the integrity, validity, or security of CFA Institute programs.
options.B: Expressing opinions critical of CFA Institute policy violates Standard VII(A).
options.C: VII(A) restricts only the disclosure of live exam questions, not other program-integrity conduct.

rationales.A: Correct. Per Standard VII(A): 'Members and Candidates must not engage in any conduct that compromises the reputation or integrity of CFA Institute or the CFA designation or the integrity, validity, or security of CFA Institute programs.'
rationales.B: Incorrect. Members may disagree with and criticize Institute policies; the standard targets integrity-compromising conduct, not opinions.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Any conduct compromising the reputation, integrity, validity, or security of Institute programs is covered.

questions.stem: Standard VII(B) Reference to CFA Institute, Designation, Program most likely:

options.A: A candidate who has registered for Level III may append 'CFA, expected 2027' to their name, because imminent completion of the Program qualifies as candidacy disclosure.
options.B: Members may represent that holding the CFA charter guarantees superior investment performance, since the designation certifies advanced competence in investment management.
options.C: When referring to CFA Institute, CFA Institute membership, the CFA designation, or candidacy in the CFA Program, Members and Candidates must NOT misrepresent or exaggerate the meaning or implications of membership in CFA Institute, holding the CFA designation, or candidacy in the CFA Program.

rationales.A: Incorrect. There is no partial designation; candidacy may be stated only factually (e.g., 'passed Level II; registered for the Level III exam').
rationales.B: Incorrect. Implying performance superiority misrepresents the meaning of the designation.
rationales.C: Correct. Per Standard VII(B): 'When referring to CFA Institute, CFA Institute membership, the CFA designation, or candidacy in the CFA Program, Members and Candidates must not misrepresent or exaggerate the meaning or implications of membership in CFA Institute, holding the CFA designation, or candidacy in the CFA Program.' Per Solution 10: Standard VII explicitly addresses 'reference to the CFA Program.'

questions.stem: Number of top-level Standards most likely:

options.A: Seven.
options.B: Six.
options.C: Eight.

rationales.A:
Full statement: seven top-level Standards: I. Professionalism; II. Integrity of Capital Markets; III. Duties to Clients; IV. Duties to Employers; V. Investment Analysis, Recommendations, and Actions; VI. Conflicts of Interest; VII. Responsibilities as a CFA Institute Member or CFA Candidate.

Correct. Per the Standards of Professional Conduct there are seven top-level Standards: 'i. PROFESSIONALISM; ii. INTEGRITY OF CAPITAL MARKETS; iii. DUTIES TO CLIENTS; iv. DUTIES TO EMPLOYERS; v. INVESTMENT ANALYSIS, RECOMMENDATIONS, AND ACTIONS; vi. CONFLICTS OF INTEREST; vii. RESPONSIBILITIES AS A CFA INSTITUTE MEMBER OR CFA CANDIDATE.'
rationales.B: Incorrect. There are seven top-level Standards, not six.
rationales.C: Incorrect. There are seven top-level Standards, not eight.

questions.stem: Best strict-law approach for I(A) when conflict exists most likely:

options.A: In event of conflict between applicable laws, rules, or regulations, must comply with the MORE STRICT law, rule, or regulation.
options.B: In a conflict of laws, members should comply with the law of their country of residence.
options.C: In a conflict of laws, the less strict law governs so long as local regulators permit it.

rationales.A:
Full statement: in event of conflict between applicable laws, rules, or regulations, must comply with the MORE STRICT law, rule, or regulation; principle applies whenever different jurisdictions or professional bodies have overlapping but inconsistent requirements — Member/Candidate must follow the higher standard.

Correct. Per Standard I(A): 'In the event of conflict, Members and Candidates must comply with the more strict law, rule, or regulation.'
rationales.B: Incorrect. Residence does not decide the question; the MORE STRICT applicable rule governs.
rationales.C: Incorrect. The stricter of the applicable laws, rules, or regulations must be followed.

questions.stem: I(A) dissociation obligation most likely:

options.A: Dissociation is required only after a regulator has formally charged the wrongdoer.
options.B: Must NOT knowingly participate or assist in and must DISSOCIATE from any violation of applicable laws, rules, or regulations.
options.C: Members satisfy Standard I(A) by merely abstaining from personally initiating the violation while continuing to work on the account.

rationales.A: Incorrect. The dissociation duty arises from knowledge of the violation, not from regulatory action.
rationales.B:
Full statement: must NOT knowingly participate or assist in and must DISSOCIATE from any violation of applicable laws, rules, or regulations; dissociation means separating from the violation — could include refusing to participate, reporting concerns, or leaving position if necessary.

Correct. Per Standard I(A): 'Members and Candidates must not knowingly participate or assist in and must dissociate from any violation of such laws, rules, or regulations.'
rationales.C: Incorrect. Knowing participation OR assistance is prohibited; continued association with the activity can itself constitute participation.

questions.stem: Consistency with client mandates under III(C) most likely:

options.A: An investment consistent with the client's verbal preferences satisfies suitability even where it conflicts with the client's written mandate.
options.B: Suitability to the client's financial situation may be confirmed after execution, provided the position is reviewed at the next portfolio rebalancing. That specification would be used as-is, with no forward-looking overlay. Applied uniformly, it would bind at every horizon and every asset class.
options.C: In advisory relationship, must determine that an investment is suitable to the client's financial situation and consistent with the client's WRITTEN objectives, mandates, and constraints BEFORE making an investment recommendation or taking investment action.

rationales.A: Incorrect. Suitability must be judged against the client's WRITTEN objectives, mandates, and constraints; verbal preferences do not override the written mandate.
rationales.B: Incorrect. The suitability determination must be made BEFORE making an investment recommendation or taking investment action, not confirmed after execution.
rationales.C: Correct. Per Standard III(C)(1)(b): 'Determine that an investment is suitable to the client's financial situation and consistent with the client's written objectives, mandates, and constraints before making an investment recommendation or taking investment action.'

questions.stem: Suitability in context of total portfolio under III(C) most likely:

options.A: In advisory relationship must judge the suitability of investments in the context of the client's TOTAL PORTFOLIO — not just in isolation.
options.B: Suitability must be judged security by security, with each holding individually matching the client's risk profile. That specification would be used as-is, with no forward-looking overlay.
options.C: Portfolio context matters only for concentrated positions above 10% of client assets.

rationales.A:
Full statement: in advisory relationship must judge the suitability of investments in the context of the client's TOTAL PORTFOLIO — not just in isolation; individual security may be inappropriate on standalone basis but suitable when combined with other holdings, or vice versa; total portfolio approach recognizes diversification and overall risk exposure.

Correct. Per Standard III(C)(1)(c): '[Members and Candidates must] Judge the suitability of investments in the context of the client's total portfolio.' Per Solution 6: Standard III(C) 'requires members and candidates in an advisory relationship with a client to... consider investments in the context of the client's total portfolio.'
rationales.B: Incorrect. Suitability is judged in the context of the client's TOTAL portfolio; an individually risky holding can be suitable within a diversified whole.
rationales.C: Incorrect. No such threshold exists; total-portfolio context always applies.

questions.stem: Standard IV(A) Loyalty prohibition scope most likely:

options.A: In matters related to their employment, must act for benefit of their employer and NOT: (1) deprive their employer of the advantage of their skills and abilities.
options.B: Skills and experience gained on the job may never be used after leaving the employer.
options.C: The loyalty standard is limited to prohibiting theft of physical employer property.

rationales.A:
Full statement: in matters related to their employment, must act for benefit of their employer and NOT: (1) deprive their employer of the advantage of their skills and abilities; (2) divulge confidential information; (3) otherwise cause harm to their employer; multiple prohibitions cover taking skills to competitor, sharing employer's confidential information, and general harmful conduct.

Correct. Per Standard IV(A): 'In matters related to their employment, Members and Candidates must act for the benefit of their employer and not deprive their employer of the advantage of their skills and abilities, divulge confidential information, or otherwise cause harm to their employer.'
rationales.B: Incorrect. Skills and experience (as opposed to confidential information and records) may be used after departure.
rationales.C: Incorrect. IV(A) also prohibits depriving the employer of one's skills, divulging confidential information, and otherwise causing harm.

questions.stem: IV(B) written consent scope most likely:

options.A: Must obtain written consent from ALL parties involved before accepting gifts, benefits, compensation, or consideration that competes with or might reasonably be expected to create conflict of interest with their employer's interest.
options.B: Consent from the employer alone is sufficient for accepting compensation offered by a grateful client. That specification would be used as-is, with no forward-looking overlay. Applied uniformly, it would bind at every horizon and every asset class.
options.C: Consent may be obtained retroactively within 30 days of accepting the benefit.

rationales.A:
Full statement: must obtain written consent from ALL parties involved before accepting gifts, benefits, compensation, or consideration that competes with or might reasonably be expected to create conflict of interest with their employer's interest; 'all parties' means not just employer — could include client and other affected parties as well.

Correct. Per Standard IV(B): 'Members and Candidates must not accept gifts, benefits, compensation, or consideration that competes with or might reasonably be expected to create a conflict of interest with their employer's interest unless they obtain written consent from all parties involved.' Per Solution 8: consent from employer only is not sufficient — Standard IV(B) requires 'written consent from all parties involved.'
rationales.B: Incorrect. Written consent is required from ALL parties involved.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Consent must precede acceptance; there is no retroactive cure period.

questions.stem: Supervisor responsibility scope under IV(C) most likely:

options.A: Standard IV(C) requires supervisors to guarantee that no violations occur.
options.B: Supervisory responsibility extends only to direct reports, not to others under the member's authority.
options.C: Must make reasonable efforts to ensure that anyone subject to their supervision or authority complies with applicable laws, rules, regulations, and Code and Standards.

rationales.A: Incorrect. The duty is REASONABLE EFFORTS to ensure compliance, not an absolute guarantee.
rationales.B: Incorrect. The duty covers anyone subject to the member's supervision OR AUTHORITY.
rationales.C:
Full statement: must make reasonable efforts to ensure that anyone subject to their supervision or authority complies with applicable laws, rules, regulations, and Code and Standards; broader than mere detection — includes creating and enforcing compliance systems, training, and taking corrective action; supervisors do NOT focus 'only on detection and prevention of violations' — broader compliance responsibility exists.

Correct. Per Standard IV(C): 'Members and Candidates must make reasonable efforts to ensure that anyone subject to their supervision or authority complies with applicable laws, rules, regulations, and the Code and Standards.' Per Solution 3: supervisors are NOT required to focus 'only on the detection and prevention of violations' — the responsibility is broader.

questions.stem: Reliance on third-party research under Standard V(A) most likely:

options.A: Prohibits reliance on any research or quantitative model the member did not personally develop.
options.B: Requires reasonable and diligent efforts to determine that third-party research and quantitative tools used in the analysis are sound.
options.C: Permits use of third-party research without review, because responsibility for its quality remains with the firm that produced it.

rationales.A: Incorrect. Third-party research and quantitative tools may be used, provided the member performs due diligence on their soundness.
rationales.B: Correct. Standard V(A) Diligence and Reasonable Basis extends to due diligence on third-party research and quantitative tools: members must have a reasonable and adequate basis, supported by appropriate research and investigation, for any investment analysis, recommendation, or action.
rationales.C: Incorrect. A member relying on secondary or third-party research must make reasonable and diligent efforts to determine that it has a sound basis; responsibility cannot be shifted to the producing firm.

questions.stem: Prompt disclosure of material process changes under V(B)(2) most likely:

options.A: Material changes to the investment process may be disclosed in the next regularly scheduled annual report.
options.B: Must PROMPTLY disclose to clients and prospective clients any changes that might materially affect the basic format and general principles of the investment processes they use to analyze investments, select securities, and construct portfolios.
options.C: Only changes that reduce expected returns require disclosure to clients.

rationales.A: Incorrect. Changes that might materially affect the process must be disclosed PROMPTLY.
rationales.B:
Full statement: must PROMPTLY disclose to clients and prospective clients any changes that might materially affect the basic format and general principles of the investment processes they use to analyze investments, select securities, and construct portfolios; not annual — must be prompt.

Correct. Per Standard V(B)(2): 'Disclose to clients and prospective clients the basic format and general principles of the investment processes they use to analyze investments, select securities, and construct portfolios and must promptly disclose any changes that might materially affect those processes.' Per Solution 4: Standards require members and candidates to 'promptly disclose changes that might materially affect investment processes.'
rationales.C: Incorrect. Materiality to the process, not the direction of expected returns, triggers disclosure.

questions.stem: An analyst's report states, without qualification, that a company 'will grow earnings 15% annually over the next five years.' Under Standard V(B)(5), this statement most likely:

options.A: Complies with the Standard, because forecasts grounded in thorough analysis may be presented as facts. That specification would be used as-is, with no forward-looking overlay.
options.B: Violates the Standard, because a forecast is an opinion and has been presented as fact without being distinguished as such.
options.C: Is acceptable, provided the analyst genuinely believes the forecast and it later proves accurate.

rationales.A: Incorrect. However thorough the underlying analysis, a forecast remains an opinion and must be distinguished from fact — for example, by framing it as an expectation or estimate.
rationales.B: Correct. Per Standard V(B)(5), members and candidates must 'distinguish between fact and opinion in the presentation of investment analysis and recommendations.' An unqualified assertion that earnings WILL grow 15% annually presents an opinion (a forecast) as fact.
rationales.C: Incorrect. The violation is presenting opinion as fact; it does not depend on the analyst's sincerity or on whether the forecast later proves accurate.

questions.stem: Conflicts of Interest historical vs current language most likely:

options.A: Standard VI(A) Conflicts of Interest historically required members and candidates to DISCLOSE conflicts but language made no mention of AVOIDING conflicts.
options.B: The current standard removed the disclosure option, mandating avoidance of all conflicts.
options.C: The historical language of the conflicts standard required avoidance of conflicts and made no mention of disclosure. That specification would be used as-is, with no forward-looking overlay.

rationales.A:
Full statement: Standard VI(A) Conflicts of Interest historically required members and candidates to DISCLOSE conflicts but language made no mention of AVOIDING conflicts; guidance for VI(A) has long stated best practice is to avoid conflicts or appearance of conflicts; including option to AVOID versus simply disclosing conflicts in language of standard emphasizes that members and candidates should avoid conflicts of interest whenever reasonably possible; although avoiding conflicts altogether is preferred, often may not be reasonable in investment industry; when not reasonable to avoid conflict, VI(A) continues to require clear and complete disclosure.

Correct. Per the reading: 'Standard VI(A) Conflicts of Interest historically required members and candidates to disclose conflicts, but the language of the standard made no mention of avoiding conflicts. Nevertheless, the guidance for Standard VI(A) has long stated that best practice is to avoid conflicts or the appearance of conflicts. Including the option to avoid versus simply disclosing conflicts in the language of the standard emphasizes that members and candidates should avoid conflicts of interest whenever reasonably possible. Although avoiding conflicts altogether is preferred, often in the investment industry it may not be reasonable for members and candidates to avoid a conflict or the perception of a conflict. When it is not reasonable for members and candidates to avoid a conflict, Standard VI(A) continues to require clear and complete disclosure of the conflict.'
rationales.B: Incorrect. Current VI(A) permits either avoiding the conflict or making full and fair disclosure.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Historically the standard required DISCLOSURE and made no mention of avoidance — the reverse.

questions.stem: A manager emails a ratings downgrade to her largest fee-paying clients first and to her remaining clients the following day. Under Standard III(B), this practice most likely:

options.A: Violates the Standard only if the clients informed later suffer measurable trading losses.
options.B: Complies with the Standard, because premium service levels for larger fee-paying clients are permitted without restriction. That specification would be used as-is, with no forward-looking overlay.
options.C: Violates the Standard, because changes in recommendations must be disseminated fairly to all clients, not sequenced to advantage selected clients.

rationales.A: Incorrect. The unfair dissemination itself is the violation; it does not depend on whether the disadvantaged clients realize measurable losses.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Differing service levels are permissible only if disclosed and only if they do not disadvantage other clients; early access to recommendation changes disadvantages the clients informed later.
rationales.C: Correct. Per Standard III(B), members and candidates must deal fairly and objectively with ALL clients when making investment recommendations and taking investment action; releasing a recommendation change to favored clients first disadvantages the rest.

questions.stem: Prominent disclosures under VI(A) most likely:

options.A: Conflict disclosures may be made in fine-print footnotes as long as they are technically accurate.
options.B: Disclosures may use technical legal language, since sophistication is presumed of all clients.
options.C: Must ensure that such conflict disclosures are PROMINENT, are delivered in PLAIN LANGUAGE, and COMMUNICATE THE RELEVANT INFORMATION EFFECTIVELY.

rationales.A: Incorrect. Disclosures must be PROMINENT; technically accurate fine print fails the standard.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Plain language that communicates the relevant information effectively is required.
rationales.C:
Full statement: must ensure that such conflict disclosures are PROMINENT, are delivered in PLAIN LANGUAGE, and COMMUNICATE THE RELEVANT INFORMATION EFFECTIVELY; not enough to bury disclosure in fine print — must be visible, understandable, and effective at conveying the conflict.

Correct. Per Standard VI(A): 'Members and Candidates must ensure that such disclosures are prominent, are delivered in plain language, and communicate the relevant information effectively.'

questions.stem: Scope of the confidentiality duty under III(E) most likely:

options.A: The employer may authorize disclosure of client information at its own discretion at any time.
options.B: Confidentiality applies to information about current, former, AND prospective clients.
options.C: Confidentiality applies only to information about current clients and ends when the relationship terminates.

rationales.A: Incorrect; the only exceptions are illegal client activity, disclosure required by law, or the client's permission — employer discretion is not among them.
rationales.B:
Full statement: confidentiality applies to information about current, former, AND prospective clients; three exceptions permit disclosure: (1) information concerns illegal activities on the part of client/prospective client; (2) disclosure is required by law; (3) client or prospective client permits disclosure; these are the ONLY exceptions to the confidentiality duty.

Correct. Per Standard III(E): 'Members and Candidates must keep information about current, former, and prospective clients confidential unless: 1. The information concerns illegal activities on the part of the client or prospective client, 2. Disclosure is required by law, or 3. The client or prospective client permits disclosure of the information.'
rationales.C: Incorrect; the duty covers current, former, AND prospective clients and does not lapse when the relationship ends.
